title: EXP-059 — Hello World Part 4 Section 1: Add Nullable FX_Picture Binary Column to FX_Items
objective: Using the native Web Client SQL Tables maintenance Form, locate exactly one existing dbo.FX_Items table and record its complete column baseline. Add exactly one column named FX_Picture with the UI's VarBinary data type, Length -1, and Is Nullable checked. Verify the new column and unchanged existing inventory before performing exactly one ordinary Save. Capture the native Save result and any displayed generated DDL without separately executing scripts. Close and reopen SQL Tables once, retrieve dbo.FX_Items again, and prove that the recovered column inventory equals the original baseline plus the single FX_Picture column with all required attributes. Finally, open FX_Items in the Web Client runtime through the native route and verify the original three records remain unchanged, without modifying the IDO or Form. Classify results as observed only.

Capture the repository starting state and distinguish pre-existing changes from EXP-059 changes.
Use the existing authenticated Web Client and the native Open > Select Form route to open the core SQL Tables runtime Form.

Filter Table Name to exact FX_Items using native filtering/F4 and establish exactly one dbo.FX_Items record.
Record the complete pre-change column inventory, including every column's Name, Data Type, Length, and Is Nullable value, with table identity visible in the evidence.
Establish that FX_Picture does not already exist, including a case-insensitive comparison.
Use the native Columns > New operation exactly once to configure one column: FX_Picture, VarBinary or the UI-equivalent Var Binary, Length -1, Is Nullable checked.
Read back the unsaved row and verify every existing column remains unchanged before Save.
Perform exactly one native SQL Tables Save after all pre-Save gates pass; capture the complete native result and any displayed generated SQL or DDL as evidence only.
Close the clean SQL Tables internal Form tab once and reopen SQL Tables once through its native Web Client route.
Refilter dbo.FX_Items and compare the recovered inventory field by field with the captured baseline.

Perform one read-only fresh opening of the FX_Items runtime Form. If a clean inherited FX_Items internal tab must first be closed, permit one ordinary close before the single opening; never duplicate an open Form.
Confirm the three original FX_Items records, values, disabled Save state, and absence of an opening-time Hello World prompt within the documented observation window.

Create or update only the EXP-059 experiment record and evidence/EXP-059/ in the repository, with screenshots, accessibility snapshots, native responses, a cumulative action audit, and a final acceptance matrix.

acceptance_checks.description: The worker reviews the required source and experiment records, captures the starting repository state, and proves that the Web Client SQL Tables maintenance Form is usable without an authentication or session challenge. Any opening prompt is captured verbatim before action; only a verified informational prompt is dismissed. Evidence: source-review notes, Web Client identity, SQL Tables heading, prompt screenshot if present, and initial audit.

Native Table Name filtering retrieves exactly one existing dbo.FX_Items table. The pre-change column inventory is complete, with Name, Data Type, Length, and Is Nullable for every existing column. No column named FX_Picture exists under an exact or case-insensitive comparison. Evidence: target-identified table grid, complete column snapshots, baseline inventory matrix, and explicit absence finding.

Exactly one unsaved new column is present under dbo.FX_Items. Its Name is FX_Picture, its selected data type is VarBinary or the native Var Binary equivalent, Length is -1, and Is Nullable is checked. All existing columns remain unchanged. Evidence: pre-Save screenshot and native property readbacks showing target table identity and all four new-column attributes, plus the baseline comparison.

Exactly one native SQL Tables Save is invoked after the pre-Save checks pass. The resulting native confirmation or response indicates success, the Form is clean with Save disabled, and no error or unexpected consequential confirmation remains. Any displayed generated DDL is captured without separate execution. Evidence: Save action audit, exact confirmation text or response, and post-Save clean-state screenshot.

The clean SQL Tables internal Form tab is closed exactly once without an unsaved-changes prompt and SQL Tables is reopened exactly once using the supported native Web Client route. Evidence: before/after Form-tab snapshots, reopened SQL Tables heading, and counted native actions.

After reopening and refiltering, exactly one dbo.FX_Items record is recovered. Its complete column inventory equals the AC-2 baseline plus exactly one FX_Picture column with VarBinary, Length -1, and Is Nullable checked. Every original column's name, type, length, and nullable flag matches the baseline. Evidence: post-reopen table identity, complete column readbacks, and a field-by-field before/after comparison.

The FX_Items Web Client runtime Form is freshly opened once through the supported native route, with any inherited clean instance handled without duplication. All three original records are visible and unchanged: dumbbell / 45 pound iron / 45.00 / EA; eggs / cage free / 6.99 / DZ; guitar / natural acoustic / 129.99 / EA. Save is disabled, and no opening-time Hello World prompt appears in the captured immediate and settled observation window. Evidence: native opening path, runtime screenshot, complete record readback, and opening-prompt audit.

The worker's cumulative audit establishes one new column, one SQL Tables Save, one ordinary SQL Tables close/reopen, no separate script execution, no IDO or Form-definition change, no business-record mutation, and no unauthorized action. Repository confinement is established with a session-start versus final file comparison or operator-provided audit, distinguishing unrelated pre-existing modifications. Evidence: action matrix, repository audit, and recorded limitations.

The final EXP-059 report contains decisive, inspectable evidence references for AC-1 through AC-8, exact successful and failed action counts, the initial and recovered column inventories, native Save-result text, any generated SQL displayed, blockers or limitations, and the final Form state. The result is classified observed only, without claiming replay verification, independent database durability, automatic IDO synchronization, or binary-image runtime support.

initial_instruction: T1 — Read-only prerequisite and baseline capture. Read AGENTS.md, hello-world-pt4.md Section 1 (00:18–01:32), and the relevant portions of EXP-049, EXP-051, EXP-058, and EXP-040. Establish the repository starting state and note pre-existing modifications. List the controlled browser tabs and identify the currently usable Web Client. Do not change the Designer or the inherited FX_Items Form. Through native Web Client Open > Select Form, open the core SQL Tables runtime Form once. If an opening prompt appears, capture its entire exact text and the offered responses before acting; dismiss with OK only if clearly informational and non-mutating. Otherwise stop. Through native Table Name filtering and F4/Filter in Place, retrieve FX_Items and establish exactly one dbo.FX_Items target. Read the existing Columns collection in full and record every existing Name, Data Type, Length, and Is Nullable value. Explicitly determine whether FX_Picture is absent, including case-insensitive comparison. Capture clear screenshots and accessibility snapshots identifying dbo.FX_Items and the complete column baseline; if scrolling is necessary, preserve overlapping rows and reconcile the inventory. Stop after the read-only baseline. Do not click Columns > New, edit properties, perform Save, close or reopen SQL Tables, or open another runtime Form during T1. Report whether AC-1 and AC-2 are established, with exact evidence paths and limitations. If the target, baseline, or safe opening-prompt disposition cannot be established within one fresh snapshot and one corrected inspection, stop with a documented blocker rather than broadening the operation.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-175814-gBsz. Rationale: EXP-058 successfully established observed FX_Items custom-event recovery and runtime behavior. The operator's next tutorial milestone is a single SQL schema extension, adapted exclusively to the factory-owned FX_Items table. EXP-049 established the table and associated IDO, while EXP-051 and EXP-058 provide existing-data and runtime comparison baselines. Adding one nullable VarBinary column with Length -1 is the smallest controlled change that advances Part 4 without changing the IDO, property classes, Form definitions, or business records. The experiment must establish the complete existing column inventory before mutation, preserve it through one Save and ordinary SQL Tables close/reopen, and confirm that the three existing runtime records remain available. This is an original observation, not a replay. | Operator review 2026-10-11: the UPDATE alternative of the SQL pattern matched the instruction text ("Create or update only the EXP-059 record"); it now requires UPDATE <table> SET. Added browser-JavaScript and Deploy/Form Sync patterns, exact_values FX_Items, FX_Picture (case-sensitive typing guard), deny_browser_javascript, editing scope. Schema change on dbo.FX_Items authorized by the AGENTS.md FX_ scope extension (operator decision 2026-10-10).
